title: Account Executive at IT Services Provider Expects DocuSign Growth to Be Driven by Renewals and Expansion
expert: Field account executive at an international IT services provider (VAR), enterprise and upper-mid-market accounts in the Northeast; Docusign ~47%–48% of his document-workflow business
verdict: The expert's Docusign-related business rose about 10.2% y/y in Aug–Oct 2026 with no meaningful churn, almost all from the installed base; new logos remain hard against cheaper Adobe and Dropbox.

Back to double-digit growth: 🟢 **Business up about 10.2% y/y**, vs 0% and +~3% from two 2026-11-06 calls and +7%–12% from the third: above most.
DBNR / renewal expansion: 🟢 **No meaningful churn**; every renewal held or expanded, vs 5% and 7% downgrades on the 2026-11-06 consulting call: **conflicting**.
🟢 **Seats up about 11%** (estimate) vs -5%–7% on the 2026-11-06 PSA-software COO call: **conflicting**.
🟡 **Like-for-like pricing up about 4%** (estimate), in line with ~3% on two 2026-11-06 calls.

changes: Business +~10.2% vs 0% (2026-11-06, PSA-software COO), +~3% (2026-11-06, consulting strategist) and +7%–12% (2026-11-06, CPA-firm director): above most.
Seats +~11% vs -5%–7% (2026-11-06, PSA-software COO) and +3%–5% (2026-11-06, consulting strategist): conflicting.
No meaningful churn vs 5% and 7% of renewals downgraded (2026-11-06, consulting strategist): conflicting.
Like-for-like pricing +~4% vs +~3% (2026-11-06, two calls): consistent.
thesis_impact: Stance (neutral; DD growth): ↑ — +~10.2% now and ~10% CY26 (estimate) from the installed base.
Stance (very competitive legacy e-sign): → — renewals solid, but Adobe and Dropbox make new-logo wins harder.
